title: When he switched to trumpet; cornet on the records
summary: He thinks he got a trumpet before Chicago but used his Jay cornet through the Hines years, always open horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Oh, one question while I think of it, you changed, I suppose, to trumpets at some time.
When did you do that, do you remember?

About what year, or what band? Let's see, my, I'm trying to think now, when I, did I get, when did I get my first trumpet? I'm, I don't know whether it was before I came to Chicago. I think, I think I, I got a trumpet before I came to Chicago. Pardon, let's see.
Did you say you used a Harry B.J. though, the cornet?
Yeah, yeah. I got that here in Chicago. Here in Chicago. You used, you liked that better than the, that was, that was, that was good. I, I liked that, that J.
That was your last horn that you had.
That, that was it, the average, that's still the last horn. Yeah, I still had that. Still the last horn. Well, now, it, it went bad and I borrowed a horn. Yeah. My, my brother-in-law had a.
So you still used the cornet then all those times?
No, because I, I, it's blue, it's all, I know.
But I mean, when you played, like with Heinz and all you, you used.
Oh, yes, yes, yes. I had the cornet. I had the cornet then, yes, that's right.
Yeah, that's, I couldn't tell you, I can't tell from the tone whether it's a cornet or a trumpet, and sometimes when you put a mute in all these, but you never used mute much

on the records. No, no, no, I didn't. It's always open horn. Open horn, open horn mostly. But you can't always tell from the record if it's a cornet or a trumpet. That's right, that's right, no, that's right. Because then there's some of those fellas can take a trumpet and blow such big tones, big round tones, why it sounds like a cornet. Yeah. Yeah. And, can't always tell.
